transcript.text: washing machine making a horrible noise

From what you have described, the most likely cause is load size / distribution (imbalance). Does it happen with every load or mainly particular loads, and is it shaking/moving, banging heavily, ticking/scraping, or making a deep rumbling/grumbling noise?
Every load now, it's a deep rumble on the spin, like a jet engine. No banging. It's quieter on the wash.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the drum bearings or something jammed between the drum and tub. With the machine unplugged and the door open, push the drum firmly down and lift it up, then rock it side to side. Does the drum feel loose — dropping, knocking or clunking — or firm with just a slight springy movement?
Yes there's a noticeable clunky up-and-down play when I lift the drum edge. Also it rumbles/grinds when I spin it by hand.
Let's see whether the machine itself can spin: take the washing out and run a spin-only programme with the drum empty. Does it spin up properly when it's empty?
It does spin when empty but it's still really loud on the spin, same jet engine noise. Is it worth fixing on a 9 year old machine?

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
It depends on the cost of repair versus buying a new machine. If the noise is caused by worn bearings, replacement is often not economical for a nine-year-old unit. The checks point to the drum bearing. To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Zanussi, model ZWF81443W off the door label. About 9 years old, cost around £350 new. Worth fixing?

[Heading: Likely cause: drum bearing]
Given the age of the machine and the likely need for a drum bearing replacement, it is generally not worth repairing. The cost of professional repair often approaches or exceeds the value of a nine-year-old appliance. The checks point to the drum bearing. I could not find a confirmed match for model ZWF81443W in our parts catalogue, so check with the manufacturer or a parts supplier using the full model number, or ask an appliance engineer to fit it.
